en.headline: Hong Kong retains Asia’s top financial hub ranking for fourth straight year
en.dek: The city placed third globally in the latest Global Financial Centres Index, scoring 756 points, one behind London and one ahead of Singapore.
body: Hong Kong has retained its position as Asia’s leading financial centre for a fourth consecutive edition of the Global Financial Centres Index, according to the 40th report released on Wednesday by Z/Yen Group and the China Development Institute.

The city scored 756 points, placing third worldwide behind New York on 761 and London on 757, and narrowly ahead of Singapore on 755. The report noted a tight race at the top amid geopolitical pressures that saw many centres’ scores ease slightly.

Hong Kong continued to lead in Asia-Pacific and held strong positions across competitiveness factors including business environment, human capital and financial sector development. The index is published twice a year and assesses more than 100 centres.

zh.headline: 香港連續第四度蟬聯亞洲金融中心榜首
zh.dek: 最新《全球金融中心指數》報告顯示，香港以756分位列全球第三，僅次於紐約及倫敦，並領先新加坡一分。
body: 英國Z/Yen集團與中國（深圳）綜合開發研究院周三公布第40期《全球金融中心指數》報告，香港連續第四度蟬聯亞洲金融中心榜首。
香港整體評分為756分，全球排名第三，僅次於紐約的761分及倫敦的757分，並以一分之差領先新加坡的755分。報告指出，在地緣政治壓力下，多個主要中心評分略為回落，頂尖位置競爭仍然緊湊。
香港繼續在亞太區領先，並在營商環境、人力資本及金融業發展等競爭力指標維持強勢。該指數每年公布兩次，評估逾100個金融中心。
